One sleepless night, Ko slips out to walk the streets. Life after dark is a revelation! When flirtatious Nazuna invites Ko to spend the night at her place in an abandoned building, he’s stoked! But then he awakens to kisses on his neck with a little too much bite to them... Is it just the delicious taste of his blood that makes her meet him night after night for late-night adventures, conversation and...naps? Or something else? Then, when a cute girl from Ko’s past shows up and competes for his attention, his budding relationship with the undead is put to the test!

Written by Garth Ennis Art and cover by Chris Sprouse & Karl Story Variant cover A by Michael Golden Variant cover B by Sprouse From the pages of the Authority comes the Midnighter, the world's most lethal weapon, in a new Worldstorm series written by Garth Ennis (PREACHER, THE BOYS) with art by the acclaimed team of Chris Sprouse & Karl Story (TOM STRONG)!

The Midnighter, returning from a mission in war-torn Afghanistan, is accosted as he enters the Carrier. Something is terribly wrong; these unseen assailants take him down too easily and then drag him though the teleportation door to an unknown location. After regaining consciousness he is given a cryptic choice: either kill a mass murderer or die!

Fan-favorite writer Keith Giffen (52) joins the acclaimed art team of Chris Sprouse and Karl Story to form the explosive new regular creative team of MIDNIGHTER! The Midnighter is the most self-assured member of The Authority; he's been called the world's best killing machine, and he knows what his job is and how to do it. He's never had any doubt about his chosen vocation…until now.

Midnighter continues to delve deeper into his mysterious past! But he's interrupted by the unexpected appearance of a new adversary, a sultry siren who has avarice on her mind — is the timing a coincidence or something more?
After the catastrophic events in Harmony, Midnighter digs deeper into the mystery surrounding Anthem. But when he is randomly attacked by a super-villain, is it just an odd coincidence?
Midnighter decides to reclaim his hometown and brings the fight to Anthem. Hopefully, when it's over, there'll still be a hometown...
Midnighter's hometown has been overrun by a private firm of professional superhero fascists…which sounds like Midnighter's idea of a good time...

Midnighter's battles with Anthem comes to a head as he must decide between a past he doesn't remember and the complete annihilation of a town he doesn't even like.

Midnighter's fight against the murderous, tyrannical Anthem goes well...but he still might lose much important to him anyway.

The new art team of Lee Garbett (HIGHWAYMEN) & Rick Burchett (BATMAN/HUNTRESS) debuts! There's a new guy in town: Assassin8, a contract killer so deadly he'll even give the Midnighter a run for his money - and his target this time is the Midnighter himself.
Assassin8, a hitman genetically designed to mimic the Authority's heroes, takes on the Midnighter...and takes him down.

Assassin8, the world's deadliest hitman and a genetic chameleon, has defeated the Midnighter and taken over his identity. Next stop: the Carrier and the rest of the Authority...and the actual target of his assignment.

Assassin8 has stolen the Midnighter's genetic code and is aboard the Carrier, taking out the unsuspecting members of the Authority. The Midnighter is the only hope...but will he be able to stop Assassin8 before the Carrier self-destructs?

After being ambushed and forcibly taken off the Carrier with a bomb implanted into his chest, The Midnighter is made an offer he can't refuse: accept the terms of a deadly mission or die. Faced with such a pleasant prospect he agrees, biding his time until he can eviscerate his tormentors. It's not until he's near completing his objective that things go all to Hell in this action-packed spectacular!

A nice finale.
You can't just hop aboard a time machine and assassinate Adolf Hitler, no matter how bad he was. The Midnighter learns the cost of breaking the laws of time the hard way.
Midnighter, on a mission to kill Adolf Hitler, finds himself closing in on history's greatest mass-murderer - in Berlin circa 1945. Can Midnighter terminate the Führer before he kills himself?

The Midnighter returns to seek revenge on the man who sent him back in time, and the results aren't pleasant! Then again, is sickening violence really the answer, when the bad guys have planted a remote-controlled bomb in your chest? Find out as 'Killing Machine' reaches its gruesome conclusion!

In the present, an old man walks up to Paulus' mansion and asks to be let inside. He has a message for Herr Paulus. Once inside and sitting in front of Paulus he tells a short story. He says that he had been in WW2 and his division had been annihilated and he had lost contact with his allies. He was surrounded by a dozen Russians and he couldn't fight them. When he was about to be killed, a man in black appeared and killed them all. He moved, danced between them, "snapping limbs and breaking jaws." Paulus asks the old man to describe his rescuer a he does. He says that the man wore a coat, a moon symbol on his chest and an executioners hood. Then the man tells Paulus what his savior had said. The man-in-black told him that in the year 2006, on this very day and time, he should go to where he was now (Paulus' house) and deliver a message. The message: "I am coming." Then he should leave. The old man follows the man-in-black's orders and leaves immediately. Herr Paulus sits in his chair and thinks.

Traveling through time in Bonnie's time-police car, Midnighter promises that he won't hurt some unnamed male. Bonnie is unsure of Midnighter's promise, but she takes it. She offers to have sex with him, but he turns her down, telling her that he's gay. She doesn't understand, explaining that in the future, there is no "gay" or "straight." Everyone has sex with everyone. Midnighter laughs, then says it's time for an afternoon's killing.

Back in the present, Herr Paulus stands in the observation room of the time chamber with his scientists and bodyguards. He asks his scientists to make sure nothing is traveling towards them through time, and they say that they can detect nothing. They also say that Midnighter can't come back on his own since he has no time machine. Paulus turns to his guards and asks them were Rourke, the head guard is. They say that he was checking the perimeter and should soon be back. Just then, repeated "Oh God's" can be heard down the hall along with "Hop you bastard!" coming from another voice. Moments later, a one-legged, no-armed, blood covered Rourke stumbles into the room and falls down. Behind him, Midnighter walks into the room carrying a sleeping child and says, "Don't say I didn't warn you."

Paulus reaches for the detonator for the bomb in Midnighter's chest, but Midnighter tells him not to. He says he can kill the boy in his arms before Paulus presses the button, and that would erase Paulus, because the boy is him, kidnapped from the past. Midnighter holds up the helmet he'd taken from Rourke and says that it controls every part of the helmets of the other guards, and one of the things the helmets regulate is temperature. Before the guards can get the helmets off, Midnighter overloads them, incinerating the men inside.

After the men are dead, Midnighter tells Paulus that he wants the bomb out of his chest, and if Paulus doesn't make his scientists do it, he'll kill him as a child. Paulus says that Midnighter is bluffing, that he won't kill a child. Midnighter stares him in the eye and asks him if he's sure. Paulus blinks first and asks Midnighter how he knows they won't kill him on the operating table. Midnighter just says that he'll have to stay awake during the whole procedure, and he does, holding the young Anton against his side the entire time.

When the bomb is out and his backup heart is back in, Midnighter kills all the doctors and scientists and blows up the mansion. He takes Paulus outside and tells him that his parents were just as evil as Hitler, and if he'd done what Paulus had wanted and saved them, the world would be even worse than it is now. When that little explanation is over, Midnighter forces Paulus to his knees and kicks his head off.

Midnighter returns the baby Anton Paulus to the time police and they fly off. Midnighter goes back to the Carrier and ignores everyone he walks by. His inner monologue says that he's not a lover, a father or a friend. He's what he was bred to be, and that's the problem.

"Every year I come here and bring my lover roses."

In feudal Japan, a forbidden romance sparks death and destruction in the lives of all who are touched by it. A brutal tale of honor, love and, above all, vengeance.

Flowers For The Sun does not pick up at the end of issue #5 of the series. It takes place in what may be an alternate reality or the past. No real explanation is given for the setting.

In feudal Japan, a man that seems to be a version of Midnighter sits on a hill in a dead forest. There are bones of many dead men around the base of the hill and a group of armed nobles and samurai around the bones. "Midnighter" tells them that he's invited them to listen to a story. As soon as they're ready to hear it, he tells them.

One morning, Midnighter awoke with no memory of who he was. He was wearing black armor and had two swords. People assumed he was a ronin, but Midnighter could never remember having a master or even being trained to fight. He found himself walking near a castle when he was attacked by more than 60 guards. He killed them all and, amazingly, came out untouched. The shogun, impressed by his skill, hired him to work for him.

While Midnighter worked on protecting the shogun's territories and the shogun tried to help Midnighter by uncovering his past, the shogun's senior minister plotted a way to get rid of Midnighter.

One day, the shogun and Midnighter were walking through the market when a man in white (Apollo) came into town. He was harassed by some drunk men who wanted to fight. Crying, Apollo tried to get them to leave him alone. They wouldn't, so Apollo raised his sword and killed them all in one single strike. The shogun sends Midnighter to talk to the man in white and he does. Apollo comes to work for the shogun and he and Midnighter soon fall in love. However, it's not meant to last.

Midnighter alone was a problem for the shogun's senior minister, but now with Apollo there, he wasn't getting enough attention. While Apollo and Midnighter are sleeping, he sends over 200 ninjas to kill them. The fight is long and hard but Midnighter survives. Unfortunately, Apollo does not. Midnighter tortures the only surviving ninja until he finds out who was responsible. He leaves the shogun's palace for a year to mourn and bury his love, but when he comes back, he drowns the minister in his own bath.

Back on the hill, which is also Apollo's grave, Midnighter tells the men gathered that every year he brings his lover flowers. Then he tells them to defend themselves. The fight is quick and at the end, a dozen hearts are resting on Apollo's grave.

Written by Brian K. Vaughan Art by Darick Robertson & Karl Story Cover by Chris Sprouse & Story Writer Brian K. Vaughan (Ex Machina, Pride of BagHdad), and guest artist Darick Robertson (TRANSMETROPOLITAN) deliver an all-out action issue examining the Midnighter's abilities from a unique perspective. He's the man who can anticipate any move to the nth degree - now we get an idea of what that means.

Note: Midnighter 7 is written in reverse order. The last page is first and the first page is last. The meaning for this becomes clear slowly as the story is told (or immediately if read in the correct order).

This issue, like the one before it, is a one shot, not the beginning of a new arc. The story started (ended) with Midnighter kissing Apollo on The Carrier as a house of cards came crashing down around them. Before that, Midnighter had walked into the room, clicked a button that set off an explosion down on Earth and walked up to Apollo and knocked the cards down. Before that, Midnighter had fallen through a Door and into a shuttle bay on the Carrier saying, "I knew that was gonna work." The next page revealed that he had fallen from high in the air above what looked to be a beach. All the while down he had been yelling for a Door. Another step back showed Midnighter flying/falling by two robots commenting on how he had just killed their friend, a scene that came up next. Before that, the three robots had been chasing Midnighter after he had jumped off of a burning building. The building appeared next with it's roof (and a helicopter on it) on fire. Right before he jumped, Midnighter had told the robots (and a woman on the roof of a building) not to follow him. Midnighter had gone to the roof (and the flaming wreckage that was his chopper) after leaving a lower level of the building and was followed by the woman and her three robot guards. Upon seeing his vehicle destroyed, Midnighter had said, "Well, I guess I saw that coming." On his way to the roof, Midnighter had jumped through a hallway filled with fire screaming and cursing and saying he should have killed someone. Before that, he had been choking the same woman that would be on the roof with him later, but he let her live. Before he had started choking the woman, Midnighter took down 10 robots like the ones that chased him off the building. Before that, Midnighter had been standing in front of the robots with he and the woman talking about how he would kill them because they were terrorists while she threatened him. The next page wraps everything up with a little monologue from Midnighter. It reads, "See, I'm one of those jerks who always skips ahead to the last page of a book before he reads it. I find a closing scene I love, then work my way back to the beginning to figure out exactly how it all went down. It's the same way my crazy brain processes every possible outcome for a battle before the first punch is even thrown. So let's cut to the chase, shall we? I've already run through a trillion potential versions of this entire day in my head, including the spectacularly banal conversation we're about to have. And I've settled on the finale that leaves your sick operation toppling like a house of cards...and me making love to my husband."

The final (first page) shows Midnighter alone saying, "Hi, I'm Midnighter. I already know exactly how this story ends."

The Midnighter is challenged by Hawksmoor to take on a different kind of mission, one with a little more humanity. Amused by the dare, Midnighter agrees, only to find that nothing ever comes easy in this nasty world we live in.

On a space station containing inhabitants infected with a deadly virus, Midnighter fights to contain a potential world-wide plague — one that will start when the satellite re-enters the atmosphere and rains down on a major metropolitan city!

Luke Cage takes the stage in his own ongoing series! Cage makes himself the ‘Hero for Hire’ for a Chicago newspaper. Cage busts the crime, while the journalists get a story! A perfect arrangement, until Luke encounters Hardcore, a dangerous mobster with an even more dangerous agenda.

Luke Cage restarts his career as a hero mercenary leaving Harlem for a fresh start in Chicago. The beginning of Luke Cage's 1992 self-titled series Cage. A nice reviving of one of the best heroes of all time.
Two heavy-hitters, one single issue! The Hulk comes to town looking for the Rhino…and some answers. But will Luke Cage be able to talk sense into an animalistic Hulk? No chance.
Cage set-up by Troop? But why? Former allies reveal their true colors, as a gang named “Trash” takes the villainous spotlight. What does Trash want with Cage?

issue_title: The Life and Death of Luke Cage
description:
Nothing will stop Cage in the pursuit of his brother and father…not even Hardcore! Luke’s closest relatives are being held hostage by this dangerous madman. Will Cage find the answers he needs before it’s too late?

An old enemy has kidnapped Luke's loved ones and put them in a death trap. Luke must rescue them all. Iron Fist shows up to help but Luke wants to pound him as well!
Cage agrees to an exchange of services for information on his father and brother. Dr. Karl Malus unleashes Coldfire!
The Tinkerer's son is now safe thanks to Cage and Dakota North. But can the same be said for Coldfire, Luke's recently transformed brother?

issue_title: The Good, the Bad and the Deadly
description:
Silver Sable and Terror guest-star! Cage joins the mercenaries-for-hire to maintain an ancient talisman.

For Love Nor Money Part 2 of 6

The Carnal Serpent awakens! Silver Sable, Terror and Cage do unholy battle.

For Love Nor Money Part 5 of 6
Details of Luke's personal life are now public domain! Crusader comes in for the kill.
Will the unbreakable Cage be able to resist psychic persuasion while battling the Homeless Killer?
This is Luke Cage as you've never seen him before – under possession by the Bogeyman! Unleashed and raving, Cage goes on a bender.

Cage is hired as a bodyguard for a rapper who’s been a recent victim of racial crime. Luke Cage vs. Hammer, a terrorist group whose prime objective is violence against minorities. Cage unleashes his A-game.

Cage has been hired as a bodyguard for a Rap artist. However, this job turns out to be more than Cage counted on when he as to face-off against the Hammers.
The Thing and Human Torch assist Cage in freeing himself of the Bogeyman!
When The Punisher guest-stars, all bets are off! Two street-level crime fighters vs. The Untouchables, Hardcore’s personal taskforce. Will Cage and Castle bring the thunder? Yes, and then some.

Dakota North’s been kidnapped by members of The Untouchables, and only Cage and Punisher have the intel to save her. But will Cage’s worst shakedown of Hardcore be enough?

Dakota is kidnapped by Kickback, Tombstone, Hardcore and Nitro. Cage must team-up with the Punisher.

issue_title: The Evil and the Cure, Part 1 of 4: Survival of the baddest!
description: Cage in Colorado! Picking up a job for Troop, Cage and Micky travel to the American West to locate a missing guardian. A sinister state trooper is much more than he seems.

issue_title: The Evil and the Cure, Part 2 of 4: Captain of Destiny
description: Luke Cage has an unwelcome blast from the past while imprisoned at a facility that’s experimenting with the Power Man serum! Innocent civilians are put through inhumane testing. Will a new generation of impenetrable Power Men and Women see the light of day? Not if Cage can help it!

issue_title: The Evil and the Cure, Part 3 of 4: The Power Principle
description: Free from his bonds at a corrupt laboratory, Luke Cage hunts down Hardcore to have him answer for his misdeeds! A super-powered struggle in the mighty Marvel manner!

issue_title: The Evil and the Cure, Part 4 of 4: Signifying Nothing
description: Stories converge and explode in this jam-packed issue! Dakota North gets closer to finding Luke’s father…but is someone else tracking the same man? Meanwhile, Cage and the West Coast Avengers divert the disaster of the Power Man serum contaminating a local water supply!
Cage is in over his head when a client distorts the truth behind a case. Enter the Rhino, a villain as impenetrable as Cage!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
description: Discover the origins of the heroic Captain Carrot and his Amazing Zoo Crew! When Superman tries to stop a mysterious beam from Pluto from attacking the Earth, an accident leads to citizens from a planet inhabited by animals to gain super powers!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: Curse of the Wuz-Wolf; The Fadeaway Crimes of the Cheshire Cheetah!
description:
Human beings are nothing but a frightening rumor to the inhabitants of Earth-C…right? Somewhere in Follywood, Mr. Wolf is embittered by the success of the Zoo Crew. As his anger rises, so does something else-a most twisted, terrifying form, one that will give our heroes their most fur-raising mission yet. Prepare, if you dare, for the tale of the horrifyingly human Wuz-Wolf!

Notes

  • This issue appears in the movie The Outsiders on the magazine shelf along with Detective Comics #521 and Fightin' Marines #166 before the scene where Dally is shot and killed. It is an error that this issue is seen because the movie The Outsiders takes place in the 1960s and this issue came out in 1982.
  • This issue was barely visible in the 1984 movie Gremlins. When water was accidentally spilled on Gizmo.

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: The Wuz-Wolf's Night to Howl / The Sinister Salamandroid!
description: The Wuz-Wolf continues his rampage! Cursed to become a terrifying human by night, Mr. Wolf has made short work of the Zoo Crew, and is about to commit the most feared crime in the United Species: he’s going to eat Pig-Iron! Can the team save their friend? Or will this be the last oink Pig-Iron ever…well, oinks?

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
description: It’s a quiet night in the Z-Building for the Zoo Crew, but the arrival of a tiny trespasser begins a new adventure! His name is the Micro-Mouse, and he will stop at nothing to avenge his father by bringing down the evil FatKat. Don’t miss this tale of power, betrayal, and cosmic carrots!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
description: The Zoo Crew have seen all manner of bizarre sights in their storied crime-fighting careers, but they’ve never yet seen anything this inexplicable: it’s snowing in Follywood! Who would cause such a thing? What do they want? Do they have any idea what this will do to traffic? His name is Cold Turkey, and if our heroes can’t stop his chilly crimes, he just might put them on ice!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
description: “Crisis on Earth-C!” Featuring the JLA—Just’a Lotta Animals! Sorry, were you expecting someone else? The arrival of Super-Squirrel, Batmouse, Wonder Wabbit, and the rest of their furry crime-fighting team has Captain Carrot shaking in his boots. Why? He created them for his comic strip, so how exactly are they standing right in front of him?

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
description: “Crisis on Earth-C-Minus!” Continuing from last issue, the Zoo Crew and the JLA (still not that one) are lost in a Multiversal limbo! Meanwhile, the villains of both teams have united to take over Earth-C-Minus. Two teams, two universes, and two destinies will collide, all in one issue!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: The Dread Tread of the Screeching Tire
description: A lot can go wrong on a movie shoot. Planes ruin the sound of perfect takes, equipment breaks just when it’s needed most, and 10-story tires demolish sets without reason or warning. Wait, what was that last one? Maybe this is above Steven Spielbird-Dog's pay grade--time to call the Zoo Crew!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: Road To Disaster! / Rabbit, Don't Run; House Of Frankenswine

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: The Great Gnudini; Here Comes The Sun!; You Scream Ice Cream!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: The Macabre Menace of the Mammal Called--Armordillo!
description: Can the newly formed Zoo Crew survive when Pig-Iron (Peter Porkchops) departs and leaves a path of destruction in his wake?

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
description: Final issue!  A bookend with the first preview (an insert in the New Teen Titans), Garfield Logan appears in this final isssue as Changeling.  He teams up with the Zoo Crew against a non-Earth-C Grodd - still a talking gorilla!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
description:
Arriving in the nation’s capital to receive an award, the Zoo Crew are informed of a new threat from a voice inside the statue of President Abraham Linkidd. Brotherhood, founder and general manager of the secret cabal known as A.C.R.O.S.T.I.C. (Arrogant Cutthroats Repeatedly & Outrageously Subverting This Innocent Country) announces that he is taking over the United Species of Animals and challenges the Zoo Crew to try and stop him.

Note: The cover is a homage and a parody of the cover of All-Star Comics #43.

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
description: Lights, camera, action! Rubberduck’s newest movie is filming in Fastback’s hometown, so the two set out with Yankee Poodle for a trip down memory lane. When they arrive, they’ll face family reunions, the pressures of show business, and of course-a swamp monster! As if that weren’t enough horror for one magazine, Captain Carrot tries to buy an apartment!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: The Secret of Easter Bunny Island!
description: What is the secret of Easter Bunny Island? The arrival of legendary fedora-clad explorer Oklahoma Bones-or rather, his very eager son, Oklahoma Bones Jr.-brings a new mystery to the Zoo Crew. Don’t miss out as they learn of alien worlds, discover ancient secrets, and face…global destruction, sunny side up?

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: The Bunny from Beyond!; Captain Carrot Faces The Tunneling Terror, Digger O'Doom!
description: It’s an Easter catastrophe! Baron Von Vermin has tricked hundreds of children hunting Easter eggs into opening space eggs, releasing yolks that hunt right back. The Zoo Crew and Oklahoma Bones (Jr.) are racing to the rescue-but will they fall before the bunny from beyond?

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: The Coming of Bow-Zar the Barkbarian!
description: The Zoo Crew are back in Follywood, ready to bask in the sun and get some well-deserved rest, but they’ve got an unexpected visitor! Ezra Hound, cartoonist and friend of Rubberduck, has a most peculiar problem. His plans to kill off his legendary character Bow-Zar have angered someone, and they want to get him first! That someone? Bow-Zar!

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: Killing Time / Squawk Loudly...And Carry A Big Grudge!
description: It’s a beautiful day in Los Antelopes, and the Zoo Crew are celebrating by testing out their brand-new Zoo-Copter (with only one or two accidents)! But when they touch down, they quickly discover that parts of the world are slowing to a halt, and no one knows why. Will they uncover the temporal trickery of the hidden Timekeeper? Or have the Zoo Crew finally run out of time?

series_title: Captain Carrot and His Amazing Zoo Crew!
issue_title: Time Varmints!; Into the Deadly Dimension of Debbil-Dawg!
description:
“…Something tells me this isn’t Grizzlyland!” Our favorite anthropomorphic adventurers have been thrown into the time stream, and getting home won’t be easy! How will Pig-Iron and Captain Carrot escape the gladiators of Roam? Can Yankee Poodle and Rubberduck defend the court of King Looey XIV? And just who is that quick-footed friend Rubberduck has met in the Second Weird War?

This issue contained a pullout Masters of The Universe Preview.

The clairvoyant Void has a premonition about the coming evil. An evil that has a name - Helspont. Jacob Marlowe and his android bodyguard, Spartan, assemble a team of metas that includes the fierce Warblade and titanic Maul. Meanwhile, Zealot and Grifter confront the always dangerous Troika. And, the exotic dancer known as Voodoo accepts a job at The Hot Spot. This issue finishes off where #1 begins and gives an inside look to the events that lead up to the first meeting of the WildC.A.T.s.

A diminutive homeless man wakes up one day and realizes he's actually an immortal alien warlord who has been at war for over a millennia. Jacob Marlowe forms the covert super-human squad known as WildC.A.T.s to battle the Daemonite hordes. As the story unfolds more and more players are drawn into the game and the stage is set for the final battle for the future of mankind.                           

The Cabal yearns to capture a young woman who has the power of the Sight, the ability to view the Daemonite form of those they possess. The Cabal, consisting of Daemonites, knows that this young woman could destroy them all. Unfortunately for them, the WildC.A.T.s are also after this young woman, Voodoo, so they could use her power to fight against the Daemonites. The two factions converge to where Voodoo works, in a strip bar near Washington DC, and battle each other. The WildC.A.Ts emerge victorious, even gaining new members in the event, but a Coda assassin detonates herself, causing everyone to seemingly explode.

The critically acclaimed X-Men team of Chris Claremont and Jim Lee are reunited for the biggest WildC.A.T.s adventure yet. Zealot begins to teach Voodoo the ways of the Coda, but their training session is cut short when a spacecraft crash lands near by. Within Zealot encounters horrors unimaginable. Meanwhile, a startling change comes over Voodoo. Plus, introducing the mysterious Huntsman and his charge, Miranda.

Zealot trains Voodoo in the ways of the Coda and how to fight and defend herself. During the training, a flying ship crashes by them and a man, Alabaster Wu, runs out from the gunfire of an alien. Zealot leaps to his aid, killing the alien, as Voodoo tends to Alabaster Wu. Zealot decides to investigate the ship as Alabaster Wu runs off and the dead body of the alien reaches out with tentacles and captures Voodoo, possessing her, but not before she summoned assistance from her teammates. Zealot finds a girl, Miranda Tai, on the ship unconscious when she is attacked by more aliens. Soon, a man named the Huntsman, who protects Miranda Tai, jumps in to help Zealot. After defeating the aliens, they make each others acquaintance and learn that Voodoo was possessed. Together, they give chase to Voodoo, who has been been chasing Alabaster Wu, who is a friend of Lord Emp and is currently seeking his assistance. The alien possessing Voodoo then uses Voodoo's connection with the WildC.A.T.s to gather them and look for Alabaster Wu. He has finally found Lord Emp and when they speak, the WildC.A.T.s arrive, believing that Alabaster Wu is setting up Lord Emp. However, before things can be resolved, Troika and Providence arrive to fight the superheroes.

"A Soldier's Story" (short story):

It tells about Soldier's first encounter with Zealot in the Korean war, 1950.

Betrayed by one of their own, the WildC.A.T.s are overwhelmed by the Troika and their new ally, the clairvoyant Providence. Worse yet, a strange and mysterious woman of power makes the scene and she could mean the end of life on this planet as we know it. Zealot recognizes her and immediately retreats, Huntsman and Miranda in tow, to get some much needed backup.

The WildC.A.T.s realize that Voodoo has led them into a trap, but not that she is actually possessed by an alien. While Zealot, Huntsman and his ward, Miranda Tai, chase after Voodoo, the WildC.A.T.s are beaten by Providence and the members of Troika. Soon Tapestry and Lord Soma arrive, the ones who have hired the alien possessing Voodoo as well as the others. Tapestry tries to steal the essence of Lord Emp, making him her pawn, so she could have power over him. It is revealed that Tapestry has a history with Zealot, who has asked for assistance from her sister Savant.

The team is down, Zealot is gravely injured, and the Huntsman is doing all he can to keep her and his charge, Miranda, one step ahead of the pursuing Troika. Luckily, the calvary has arrived in the form of the Soldier, Savant, Grifter, and the super powerful Mister Majestic!

Zealot has been poisoned by the claw of an alien that is slowly turning her into the same kind of alien and Huntsman, with his ward Miranda Tai, travels with her when they are greeted by Troika, three powerful super-villains. Meanwhile, Tapestry has taken control of the rest of the WildC.A.T.s, making them her loyal servants. The only one to fight against it is Voodoo, who was actually possessed by an alien force. She is soon found by employees of Lord Emp. While Huntsman deals with Troika on his own, Zealot's reinforcements arrive in the form of Soldier, Mister Majestic and her younger sister, Savant. They defeat Troika and prepare to fight against Tapestry and their possessed teammates.

"HellC.A.T.s" (conclusion of a 4-issue story arc):

The reinforcements that Zealot has called in, including Huntsman and Grifter, take on Tapestry's soldiers, who are really the WildC.A.T.s possessed. The battle wages for some time as Zealot takes the fight directly to Tapestry. Their battle would lead to a stalemate if not for the intervention of Miranda Tai and the item she has taken from Savant's satchel. They are able to defeat Tapestry, who is whisked away by her servant Soma. Zealot is imbued with the power of a god after the battle and she realizes she cannot keep it, so she has Voodoo (who has recently exorcised the alien presence within her) use her power to exorcise Zealot's godhood. Voodoo is also able to 'heal' her teammates that were being possessed by Tapestry's power.

"The Price" (short story):

The story of Zealot selling herself to Tapestry, in exchange for Savant's life.

Maul learns on the news that someone close to him has been injured by Mighty Man of Freak Force. Maul visits the hospital to see his friend when he finds Mighty Man there as well. Maul immediately attacks Mighty Man and his teammates arrive to help him out. Meanwhile, WildC.A.T.s also arrive and a large battle ensues. The Savage Dragon arrives to calm things down and Maul's friend tells Maul how it wasn't Mighty Man's fault that she was injured. The two teams decide to be amicable and even go on vacation together.

The WildC.A.T.s gather in Aspen, Colorado because Emp was called there to be part of an energy committee. He tells his team that they could enjoy some free time in Aspen or wherever they would like. Just then, a helicopter attacks their abode, guns blazing through the windows and walls. Meanwhile, Ben Santini is the head of the Black Razors and has the mission of protecting the industrial leaders that are part of the energy committee because they are being targeted by Daemonites. While the Black Razors enjoy some down time before their mission, one of them is attacked by some Daemonites. The team go on their mission and protect an industrialist from a Daemonite attack. After the battle, the Black Razors learn that a Daemonite with shape-shifting abilities is masquerading as a member of the WildC.A.T.s to get close to Emp, to kill him.

Ben Santini, the leader of the Black Razors, reveals to his priest that he fears that he will kill the man that injured him many months ago, Lord Emp. The Black Razors then undergo their mission, to stop the Daemonites from attacking important industrialists, and find out that a Daemonite with shape-shifting abilities is masquerading as a member of the WildC.A.T.s. The Razors attack the WildC.A.T.s in the hope of exposing the masquerade. They eventually learn that Maul is the one being impersonated and Ben Santini is left with a problem: attack the Daemonite or kill Lord Emp, the man he blames for the misery in his life. He shoots the Daemonite and lets the WildC.A.T.s to ponder where the real Maul is.

The members of the WildC.A.T.s scour the continent in search of their missing teammate, Maul. They have learned recently that a shape-shifting Daemonite has taken the role of Maul and the ruse was recently uncovered. The WildC.A.T.s knew that the Cabal was involved with the Maul impersonation so they attack several Cabal strongholds while Void is able to hack into computer systems to find anything about the real Maul's whereabouts. Void finally learns that Maul is being held by Stormwatch and uses her teleportation abilities to gather her teammates and also free Maul. Meanwhile, a Daemonite leader, Lord Defile, resurrects Mister White, the Daemonite with shapeshifting abilities that impersonated Maul.

issue_title: Hard Hunt; Savant in "Wedding Day Jitters"
description:
Story 1

Void prepares to enter the mind of Voodoo, who has been in a comatose state for some time. Meanwhile, Grifter is battling Daemonites so he can find out who was the one behind ordering a shape-shifting Daemonite to infiltrate the WildC.A.T.s. He learns from his interrogation that the one behind it is Hightower, a Daemonite the WildC.A.T.s have crossed paths with in the past. While Grifter continues his search, Void goes through Voodoo's psyche, helping her battle whatever is causing her to remain comatose, and succeeding. Grifter calls his teammates, telling them that he has learned that Hightower is going to meet some Coda assassins in Washington, DC.

Story 2: Wedding Day Jitters

A back-up story involving a past adventure of Savant.

issue_title: Hard Hunt; Savant in "Wing and a Prayer"
description:
Story 1: The Hunt

The WildC.A.T.s arrive in Washington, DC, in a restaurant that is actually a front as a base for the Coda. Hightower is meeting some Coda, to hire them, when the WildC.A.T.s attack. Void teleports all the innocent customers out of there, but the sheer amount of people proves to be too much and collapses in fatigue. She then gets a sudden vision of the future, involving people she is not even affiliated with. Meanwhile, Hightower leaves the restaurant and the Coda fight the WildC.A.T.s, and the Coda finds themselves losing. They retreat to the cellar where they will detonate a bomb, and it explodes. However, the WildC.A.T.s survive the explosion, but are faced by Stormwatch.

Story 2: Wing And A Prayer

A back-up story involves a past adventure of Savant.

Psionic backlash from the Cat's passing blows their cover. The government can't have rogue Action Teams roaming the countryside so they send their elite enforcers - the Black Razors - to bring down the WildC.A.T.s. 1st appearance of the Troika (cameo) and Master Gnome. 1st appearance of Black Razor (think Boba Fett on steroids), the armored special forces unit put together to deal with meta humans.

Story 1: Revelations

I/O leader, John Lynch, investigates the explosion that occurred near Washington, D.C. and finds Void teleporting in with the team of WildC.A.T.s. They then immediately teleported away, back to Emp's headquarters at the Halo company. Once there, they inform Voodoo about what's going on, how two alien forces, the Daemonites and the Kherubium, have been at war and have spread it, in secret, to the planet Earth. The Deamonites have the ability to possess other beings while the Kherubium have bred with Earthlings, granting people with superhuman powers. Before too long, John Lynch sends the Black Razors to infiltrate the WildC.A.T.s. and Lynch asks for their assistance. They soon learn, thanks to Voodoo, that the Vice President of the United States is actually a Daemonite and have to stop him. Unfortunately, the Vice President is being protected by members of Youngblood, a superhero force team. In the shadows, Gnome is pleased that he has planned all this to his benefit.

Story 2: Wetworks

This story introduces the Wetworks.

The WildC.A.T.s tangle with Hightower, who implores them for assistance. He explains how he is searching for a key that could power up the Daemonite starship and wants the WildC.A.T.s to help him find it. He continues to explain that a Daemonite named Lord Defile is also searching for the keys and wants to destroy the planet with the technology on the starship. Lord Emp agrees to team up with Hightower and Grifter quits the team in disgust. Meanwhile, it seems that Savant may have one of the keys and Mister White, with some members of the Mercs, comes to retrieve it. Fortunately, Mister Majestic arrives to help her and defeats the Mercs. Union then arrives, challenging Mister Majestic to a fight.

With the WildC.A.T.s off the planet and believed dead, Savant and Mr. Majestic decide to create their own team of WildC.A.T.s to continue the cause. The roster of this new team is significantly more dangerous and unsavory than the previous incarnation, but that's the kind of brutality that Savant believes would work well for the team. To recruit their last member, Ladytron, Savant and the others investigate a restaurant that is the setting for a drug deal. They are able to get Ladytron, as well as a criminal with knowledge of crime activity on the East coast, though they had to knock Ladytron out.

Zealot, Lord Emp, Voodoo, Void, Warblade and Maul arrive on Khera and some find it a bliss while others find it a burden. Voodoo is found to have Daemonite genetics and is forced to live with other Daemonites in a secluded, underground area. Emp and Zealot are taken to be aristocrats and are being pampered by their Kheran underlings. Meanwhile on Earth, Savant and her crew are trying to transition Ladytron onto the team, but in virtual reality, every time she wakes up, she kills the team. With more trials, they are hoping she will be able to become an associate.

Void investigates the going-ons in the planet of Khera and searches for Voodoo. Every person she asks has no idea where Voodoo could be, believing that she was probably in some bar or dancing somewhere. When she asked Spartan, he informed her that she was probably in the isolated area underground. Void checked to find Voodoo there in a kind of slum area where other Daemonites where. Voodoo informs Void that the war between the Kherubium and the Daemonites has been over for 300 years, but no one knew about it. Meanwhile, on Earth, Savant's WildC.A.T.s attack H.A.R.M. of Troika, believing he is the brains of the trio. Condition Red shoots H.A.R.M., killing him.

Maul learns more about his heritage and where his kind fits into the hierarchy of Khera. "Earthside!" Story by Alan Moore. Art by Jason Johnson and Tom McWeeney. Meanwhile back on Earth, has Savant and her new team gone too far? Have they crossed a line when they crash a villain's funeral in order to take down more bad guys? Includes a pinup of Voodoo by Travis Charest and Troy Hubbs.                               

Voodoo explains to Warblade about the war between Kherubims and Daemonites and how it has been over for nearly 200 years. Meanwhile, Maul greets other beings just like him, known as Titans, and challenges one to a duel and wins. He doesn't realize the battle was for the right to have the challenger's sister, Glingo. When he arrives at his accommodations, he sees Voodoo, Warblade and Void looking particularly sad over the events of the planet. Meanwhile on Earth, Savant's team infiltrates H.A.R.M.'s funeral ceremony being held in a church reserved for cyborgs.

In light of last issue's events, Majestic begins to question if he made the right decision in sanctioning this new team of WildC.A.T.s. Is the next generation of heroes too violent for this traditional hero. When did the colors of black and white merge into shades of grey? "...as it is in Heaven!" Story by Alan Moore. Art by Travis Charest and Troy Hubbs. Meanwhile on Khera, when the team confronts Zealot, now going by her Khera name Zannah, and Marlowe, now going by Lord Emp, with the truth about the war and the planet's state of affairs they are shocked by the indifference they are met with. Can this truly be the end of the WildC.A.T.s.

Savant's WildC.A.T.s capture Slag, Attica and Deathtrap and hold them in their facility. Tao is able to use his computer knowledge to place their prisoners in a virtual reality program where they can be detained without any problems. Meanwhile, Hellstrike of Stormwatch learns that the new WildC.A.T.s have attacked H.A.R.M.'s funeral to captured Deathtrap and he gets upset, saying how Stormwatch was prepared to capture Deathtrap and his Mercs in a week. He rushes off in a drunk anger to attack the WildC.A.T.s and he realizes he bit off more than he can chew. Tao then gives Hellstrike a tracker to track down Deathtrap, who escaped during the melee. After the Stormwatch member leaves, Tao reveals to his teammates the the tracker was actually a tracer to keep tabs on Stormwatch. Meanwhile, on Khera, Voodoo, Void, Maul and Warblade realize that Emp and Zealot are too much embroiled in Kherubim politics and being treated like aristocrats to see any of the injustice on the planet. Emp and Zealot turn their back on their teammates and their teammates realize it is time to do something about their predicament.

Spartan does some midnight investigating and learns that there is something afoot on the planet of Khera. "Earth!" Story by Alan Moore. Art by Dave Johnson. Meanwhile back on Earth, the criminal underworld declares war on Savant and her team of WildC.A.T.s.                                           

Spartan overrides some of his protocols so he could revert to his old self, the concerned member of the WIldC.A.T.s. He checks up on Void and Warblade, who inform him that Voodoo has quit the team and Maul is underground with his fellow Titans. Spartan visits Maul, then Voodoo, finding answers to the problem of something on Khera breaking up the team. He realizes he needs to speak to Zealot, so he goes to her palace. Zealot is asleep when he arrives there but Spartan overhears two members of the Coda plotting a conspiracy for the next day in the Senate, where they will bomb both Zealot and Emp and blame it on the Titans. That way, the Coda could take control of the Kherubim Senate. Before he can leave, the Coda find him and disrupt his memory. Voodoo finds him some time later, damaged in the Daemonite ghetto. Meanwhile, on Earth, a gathering of super-villains view some footage of the new WildC.A.T.s in action and realize what a viable threat they are and plan to do something about it.

The Cats uncover a conspiracy on Khera to murder Zealot and Marlowe, and their deaths will be blamed on the Titans. Can they save their friends and stop this madness or is it already too late? "Earth!" Story by Alan Moore. Art by Dave Johnson and Dexter Vines. Back on Earth, the mob decides it's time to rub out Max Cash. But they soon realize that is a task easier said than done. Especially when Maxine Manchester a.k.a. Ladytron is on the scene.                              

Lord Emp and Zealot are in the Senate, in opposition, running for their political party. Maul is in attendance with his love interest, Glingo, and the others to hear the delegates speeches. Meanwhile, Voodoo brings the body of a recuperating Spartan to Warblade and Void, explaining what occurred to him and how he has lost his memory. Thankfully, they meet someone who could fix Spartan up and he does. Void teleports them to the Senate, to stop the Coda's conspiracy in killing both Zealot and Lord Emp, making Zealot a martyr for the Coda cause as well as blaming the Titans for the bombing. Glingo, learning about the treachery against the Titans, decides to grab the bomb and sacrifices her life so that there wouldn't be war. Lord Emp realizes what's going on and decides to leave the planet of Khera with his friends. Meanwhile, on Earth, Tony Twist's mobsters try to kill Condition Red, but they fail, thanks to the appearance of Ladytron.

The original team - Spartan, Zealot, Marlowe, Void, Voodoo, Maul, and Warblade - return from their trip to Khera, and they are forever changed. Can the WildC.A.T.s survive as a team after the revelation that the war with the alien Daemonites has been over for centuries. Plus, a bomb puts Max Cash in the hospital. The first shots of a super hero/villain war have been fired!            

Zealot, Spartan, Lord Emp, Void, Voodoo, Warblade and Maul are on their spacecraft back to Earth, pondering what their life will be like when they return. Meanwhile, on Earth, Savant's team of WildC.A.T.s are dealing with the crime war called upon them by a collective of super-villains. After battling some Zombots, Condition Red and Ladytron go to a bar with a superhero clientèle. Soon Condition Red views a man enter the bathroom with a briefcase and leave. A bomb explodes, destroying the bar, and giving Condition Red a concussion. Ladytron informs the rest of her team of the situation and, since some members of Stormwatch were also in the bar at the time of the explosion, they hold a meeting with Stormwatch on how to fight this crime war. In the middle of their meeting, the original WildC.A.T.s arrive at their headquarters.

Fire from Heaven: Chapter 7. Cameos by Stormwatch and Deathblow. Story by Alan Moore. Art by Travis Charest, Ryan Benjamin, JD, and Rich Friend. The original WildC.A.T.s have returned from Khera disillusioned and on the verge of dissolution. Voodoo leaves the team. And, Grifter reunites with the members of Team 7 for one final assault on Gamorra Island.

Story continued from Sigma #2.

Story continues in Deathblow #27.

The original WildC.A.T.s arrive in time to assist Savant's team in their crime war, but many of them have decided to leave the team instead. Lord Emp and Voodoo go off on their own. Grifter arrives to see his old team, but leaves immediately to handle some business in Gamorra Island involving his old team, Team 7. When Zealot hears that Grifter has left to Gamorra Island, she gathers the old team and goes after him. Savant's team fights in the middle of the streets against the crime collective, and the war gets out of hand.

The action heats up. As Zealot, Warblade, and Grifter confront the Daemonite Warlord, Helspont and his henchmen, the rest of the team is locked in mortal combat with the government's elite super-human strike force, Youngblood. Meanwhile, Master Gnome and the villainous Troika move into position for the endgame.

Youngblood faces off against WildC.A.T.s, as the WildC.A.T.s realize the Vice President of the United States is actually an evil Daemonite and will do anything to stop him. Since Youngblood is the VP's personal bodyguards, the ensuing fight is catastrophic. WildC.A.T.s try to inform the members of Youngblood of the VP's true self, but they are not willing to believe it. Meanwhile, some other WildC.A.T.s find Helspont and stop him from trying to take over the planet. Voodoo is able to exorcise the Daemonite from the Vice President's body, causing the battle between them and Youngblood to stop. However, Helspont has started to open a portal to allow more Daemonites to come to Earth so they can all take it over.

Fire from Heaven: Chapter 13. Guest-starring Stormwatch, Team 7, Gen 13, and Union. Story by Alan Moore. Art by Travis Charest and Ryan Benjamin. Savant and Tao are up to their ears in super-villains back in New York. Meanwhile, the heroes of the Wildstorm Universe unite for the ultimate battle. Plus, the return of a fallen hero from the past.

Story continues from StormWatch 36.

Story continues in Sigma #3.

The new WildC.A.T.s recent aggressive tactics have had subversive effects. They now find themselves under siege by a criminal underworld that has declared war on them. Do even Majestic and Savant's team combined with the original Cats and Stormwatch have the power and resources to quell such an uprising? Especially when the super-cyborg, Overt-Kill, arrives on the scene. Plus, a traitor in their midst stands revealed.

Villains have united all over the city and declared war on the WildC.A.T.s. With all the turmoil within, can the team set aside personal differences long enough to quell this uprising? Featuring a knock-down-drag-out battle between Maxine Manchester and the cyborg killing machine known as Overt-Kill you have to see to believe. Plus, the traitorous Tao makes his move.
The WildC.A.T.s are locked inside their headquarters with arguably the most dangerous man alive. This is a confrontation not everyone will walk away from intact.

The devious Tao has turned Maxine Manchester into a walking nuclear bomb. The city is moments away from final annihilation and the only way to save it may mean the WildC.A.T.s have to end the life of one of their own.

An immensely powerful warrior by the name of Crusade, whose sole purpose is to hunt down and kill aliens, attacks, and not even Majestic and Zealot maybe strong enough to defeat him. Luckily, Union drops by to lend a hand.
The immensely powerful warrior known as Crusade has declared war on the WildC.A.T.s. The hero Union has arrived on the scene, but is he here to help the Cats, or his former ally, Crusade?

issue_title: Survival Of The Species, Part. 1 : Hunting Season!
description: With half the team leaving, tensions continue to boil between Grifter and John Colt over the affections of Zealot. Plus, Max Cole uncovers a conspiracy that could change the landscape of humanity for all time.

issue_title: Survival Of The Species, Part. 2 : Hits and Mythos
description: Last issue saw the revelation of the Puritans, a secretive and highly technologically advanced organization whose sole purpose is to eradicate all Kherubim and Daemonites from the face of the earth. Can Max Cash get to his brother, Grifter, in time to warn the Cats of the coming danger. What deadly secret does the Coda trained Olympia hide? Plus, introducing two new players, Mythos, the immortal human weapon, and Eve, a young woman brimming with immense psionic power.

issue_title: Survival Of The Species, Part. 3 : Predator & Prey
description: The mysterious Coda trained Olympia's secret is revealed. And, Zealot challenges her to a dual to the death. Plus, the Puritans enact an all out assault on the WildC.A.T.s' headquarters.

The Daemonite Warlord known as Helspont stands at the cusp of total victory. Soon he'll be joined by hordes of his alien Daemonite brethren. The only thing standing in the way of Earth and Armageddon is the WildC.A.T.s.

Youngblood and some members of WildC.A.T.s join together to stop Helspont from bringing his fellow aliens, the Daemonites, to Earth so they could conquer it. Helspont proves to be a formidable foe and is able to rebuff their attack. The rest of the WildC.A.T.s team regroups and give chase to Helspont, leading to a massive battle. Helspont reveals he has a power orb that could power up the transport of his fellow Daemonites when the Gnome and his Triad arrives to steal the orb, blasting Helspont out of the fray. Knowing the orb is too powerful to be allowed in anyone else's hand, Emp blasts the Gnome's arm off and the orb falls down. The Gnome chases after him and the whole facility they are in explodes. Youngblood is able to escape and ponder the fate of the WildC.A.T.s.

The issue ends with a short preview of Larry Stroman's "The Tribe" (Image, 1993).

issue_title: Survival Of The Species, Part. 4 : Fight Or Flight
description: The Puritans attacked the WIldC.A.T.s on their home turf, now it's their turn to repay the favor. But when the team storms the Puritan's headquarters they learn the disturbing magnitude of the organization's plans. They plan to travel back in time to when the Kherubim and Daemonite first arrived on Earth and destroy the alien bloodline before it can begin.

issue_title: Endangered Species, Part. 1 : For Whom the Bell Tolls...! / Recruitment
description: The Puritans, a highly technologically advanced organization out to eliminate all Kherubim and Daemonites from the planet, plan to rewrite history. If the WildC.A.T.s want to continue to exist they'll have to follow Gina and her elite strike team on a dangerous trek back through time. First stop...smack dab in the middle of World War I. "Recruitment!" Story by Brandon Choi. Art by Carlos D'Anda. Get a look at how the Puritans recruited some of the highly skilled operatives.

issue_title: Endangered Species, Part. 2 : Brothers In Arms
description: As the WildC.A.T.s pursue the Puritans back through time they find themselves in the middle of World War I. There two Red Cross soldiers with familiar faces (Ernest Hemingway and Frank Cash, Grifter and Max's grandfather) help them avoid the Axis troops. But things get worse when they discover a Daemonite warlord plans to turn the tide of the war by unleashing toxic gas!

The WildC.A.T.s adventure back through time continues and they next find themselves in the Himalayan Mountains and cross paths with a certain explorer by the name of Marco Polo. It's on these snow cape peaks that, after a near death experience, Olympia and Max Cash discover they have a growing affection for one another.

700 years in the past, the WildC.A.T.s arrive in fabled Shangri-La, but soon learn sinister elements are afoot. If the Cats and the explorer Marco Polo are to survive their visit, one of the team members will have to make the ultimate sacrifice.

Sister Eve has made the ultimate sacrifice so that her teammates can continue their pursuit of the Puritans, a secret cabal who are hellbent on traveling back through time and destroying the Kherubim and Daemonite bloodlines at their source. Next stop...ancient Rome and the Coliseum! Plus, the surprise return of a villain from the WildC.A.T.s past.

Can the Cats survive a stint as gladiators? Maybe with a little help from a certain super-powerful Kherubim Lord. What is the diabolical Helspont doing in ancient Rome? Plus, will another member of the team fall by the wayside?

The Puritans, a highly technologically advanced organization, has sent an elite strike force back in time to eradicate the Kherubim and Daemonite bloodlines from the face of the planet forever. Hot on their heels, the WildC.A.T.s arrive in the far flung past onboard the very space vessel that brought the Kherubims to planet Earth. Get an insightful look at characters like Zealot, Marlowe, Savant, and Majestic as they were thousands of years ago.

It's an all out war between the Kherubim and the Daemonites. Stuck in the middle of it all are the WildC.A.T.s desperately trying to prevent the Puritans from changing the course of history. This penultimate issue to the Cat's biggest adventure has action, intrigue, and more character defining moments than you can shake a stick at.

It all comes to a head. Gina, an operative of the Puritans, has made it back to the dawn of time when aliens first arrived on Earth. Will she succeed in destroying the Kherubim and Daemonite bloodlines forever, or can the WildC.A.T.s, who have already lost two members on their trek back through time, stop her? It's an action packed and explosive conclusion to the biggest WildC.A.T.s adventure of all time!

When the WildC.A.T.s set out to stamp out a Daemonite nest the team finds themselves caught in the middle of an old vendetta between Warblade and the woman called Misery.

The WildC.A.T.s invade a facility that is housing some Daemonites. The leader of this group has a host that was involved with the super-team known as Cyberfoce. The leader has an aide in Misery, a telepathic woman with very formidable fighting prowess. When she meets Warblade, it is revealed that they both have a past together, a very close and turbulent one. While the rest of the team battles and defeats the Daemonites, Warblade insists that he will stay behind to stop Misery. Soon, unfortunately, the whole base explodes, and the WildC.A.T.s are left wondering if their teammate could have survived it.

Final issue. In three separate yet related tales the WildC.A.T.s bring closure to many of their loose ends while setting the stage for their future. "Old Feelings!" Story by James Robinson. Art by Jim Lee and Scott Williams. Spartan and Voodoo discuss their past and future together on the team. All while in the middle of a life or death battle with the villainous Slag. "The Last Goodbye!" Story by Brandon Choi and Jonathon Peterson. Art by Ed Benes, Al Vey, and JD. Max Cash says his final goodbyes before expiring. Grifter tracks down his brother's assassin and learns this was a vendetta that reached across the sands of time. "Reincarnation!" Story by Alan Moore. Art by Travis Charest and JD. Savant, Grifter, Majestic, and Maxine Manchester are confronted by a forgotten villain. Plus, the seeds for the future are planted. Includes and afterward by Jim Lee, a 4-pages preview sketchbook for the new Wildcats series by Scott Lobdell and Travis Charest, and a pinup of the team by Scott Williams. Cover by Jim Lee and Scott Williams.

The WildC.A.T.s and the cyborg mutants of Cyberforce find themselves at odds, especially the razor fisted heroes Warblade and Ripclaw. And it's all because of the woman named Misery. Story continues in Cyberforce (1993 2nd Series) #2.

After the events of the last issue where a facility in Gamorra exploded, Gamorran airships come to investigate and attack the WildC.A.T.s. They are blasted out of the sky but the WildC.A.T.s are able to recover, with everyone on the team making it to the ground without being harmed much. Void teleports Voodoo back to the headquarters, due to her injuries, while the rest of the team search the facility to find their teammate, Warblade. They soon find Misery in the wreckage, taking Warblade with her. She soon teleports out with their teammate and they find a stasis pod in the wreckage, something Misery was trying to get before the WildC.A.T.s returned. Misery ends up with Warblade off the coast of Gamorra, on the Isle of the Dead. Warblade, upon gaining consciousness, attacks Misery but is stopped in his tracks when Ripclaw from Cyberforce arrives, ready to battle for Misery and under her telepathic thrall.

Continued in Cyber Force #2.

Story continued from Cyberforce (1993 2nd Series) #2. It's all out war as the WildC.A.T.s and the cyborg mutant heroes of Cyberforce are manipulated into a no holds barred battle by the machinations of the woman called Misery. What is the secret from the past that connects Warblade and Ripclaw to this mysterious woman, and why are they willing to kill each other for her? Story concludes in Cyberforce (1993 2nd Series) #3.

Cyberforce arrives at the Isle of the Dead to investigate where the WildC.A.T.s are. Due to Misery's telepathy clouding Cyberforce's minds, they believe that the WildC.A.T.s are part of the Cyberdata and are bio-synthetic organisms created to cause trouble. WildC.A.T.s and Cyberforce battle on the island and Ripclaw and Misery are able to escape the melee, finding the technology that Misery really wanted from the island. Before they could escape, Warblade arrives for one final battle.

Continued in Cyber Force #3.

In the aftermath of the events of Killer Instinct, the team is in need of some much needed R&R, but things don't always go according to plan. While on an ocean cruise the WildC.A.T.s are suddenly, and violently, ripped from this world and pulled into the unknown. Meanwhile Grifter receives an ominous message an sets out on his own.

Story 1: "Down Time"

The members of WildC.A.T.s enjoy some down time. Zealot and Grifter spend time in a bar, playing pool and getting into fights. Soon Grifter is summoned and leaves Zealot behind, telling him that it's a personal matter he has to attend to. Warblade and Maul visit an art gallery and meet some girls. Voodoo and Spartan enjoy a vacation on a cruise ship along with Emp. They pass the Bermuda Triangle and the whole ship is sucked into a vortex. Void is able to sense that Lord Emp is in trouble and summons her fellow teammates to investigate. Meanwhile, Spartan, Voodoo and Lord Emp are met by Lord Entropy, someone from Lord Emp's past, though he has no recollection of it.

Story 2: "Passed Lives"

Voodoo goes back to dancing and is attacked by Devin, the Coda assassin that tried to capture her and was caught in an explosion. Voodoo is able to defend herself and Devin dies on her own blade.

An ancient foe from Marlowe's past has come seeking revenge. Will Spartan and Voodoo pay for crimes Lord Emp committed centuries ago? Or can the rest of the team arrive in time to save the day? Plus, Warblade stars in "The Bonds of Blood & Steel!

Lord Entropy has Lord Emp, Spartan and Voodoo captive and the rest of their teammates are searching for them. Lord Entropy explains how he was waiting for this time to enact his revenge on Emp, but Emp has no memory of Lord Entropy. Lord Entropy explains in the medieval times they were soldiers and partners and they had a mission to save Lord Entropy's wife from Brannach the Black. They were able to defeat Brannach, who was possessed by a Daemonite, but the Daemonite then possessed Lord Entropy's wife. Emp was forced to kill her and Lord Entropy never forgave Emp. The WildC.A.T.s arrive and are able to defeat Lord Entropy with teamwork. After the battle, Lord Emp reconsiders leading the WildC.A.T.s and reveals to void that Entropy was his brother.

series_title: Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures (Phase III)
description: "Out here at the edge of the war… death surrounds us." It has been one year since the fall of Starlight. Padawan Lula Talisola and many others are missing and presumed dead. At the Almohaj Cantina, a Republican Outpost on the planet of Eriadu, Zeen mourns… and waits. When an intriguing transmission is received from Tartak Vil, a warlord on the remote moon of Bracront, Zeen, Qort, and a void-contemplating droid named 5AG3 must venture once more into hyperspace to repair their fractured team and, perhaps, the galaxy.

series_title: Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures (Phase III)
description: More all-ages adventures set in the period of the High Republic! Zeen, Lula, and their friends come face-to-face with a familiar nemesis on the streets of Eriadu City! As the Republic and the Jedi try to protect the capital from capture, they must do battle with old enemies. The fate of the planet is on the line as the forces of light and dark vie for its allegiance!

series_title: Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures (Phase III)
description: Eriadu is under siege! The fate of the planet lies with the ruling Tarkin family, and nobody knows whose side they’re on. Will the Tarkins join forces with the Republic resistance or capitulate to the vile Nihil? While the bureaucrats wheel and deal, Padawan Ram Jomaram gathers a team of underdogs to launch a rescue mission deep within the Occlusion Zone! Artist Caio Filipe, the illustrator of Lotus Land, joins the High Republic Adventures saga for the first time!

series_title: Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures (Phase III)
description: The Nihil are closing in on Valo and a mysterious pirate radio broadcaster known as the Scarlet Skull has called for help. Padawan Ram Jomaram and Jedi Knight Farzala Tarabal have bravely answered the distress call, but soon find themselves in over their heads. Will Ram, Farzala, and the Scarlet Skull mange to save Valo from the Nihil... again?

series_title: Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures (Phase III)
description: Padawan Ram Jomaram and Jedi Knight Farzala Tarabal have begun gathering brave fighters to repel the Nihil invasion of Valo. But uniting the war-weary people to defend their home is proving to be a battle all its own. Will the Jedi and their allies be able to inspire a resistance in the face of such destruction? Meanwhile, a shocking discovery on Eriadu inflames tensions!

series_title: Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures (Phase III)
issue_title: The Jedi and the Warden, Part 1
description: Fighting erupts on Eriadu! After months of oppression by the dastardly Nihil, valiant partners Lula and Zeen lead the charge against the occupying force. Meanwhile, a hidden danger stirs beneath the battlefield that threatens to turn the tide of the war, but in whose favor? The fate of the galaxy is on the line as the final arc of The High Republic Adventures begins!

series_title: Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures (Phase III)
issue_title: The Jedi and the Warden, Part 2
description: Eriadu is a battleground! Qort, Farzala, and their allies fight valiantly against the Nihil as they vie for control of the planet and the galaxy! But our heroes’ brave yet meager fighting force is drastically outnumbered by Marchion Ro’s vast army, bolstered by merciless droids and savage war beasts. Will help arrive for the forces of light and life before they are overwhelmed?

description: Zeen, Jedi Knight Qort, and droid 5A-G3 have been following every clue to find answers about their friends who are missing-and presumed dead-since the Starlight Beacon disaster. Together with an assemblage of battle-ready Jedi, smugglers, and pirates, they've got a new lead to pursue and it is taking them straight to a Nihil prison ship... Dare they hope to discover surviving allies there?

Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures (Phase III)

After their reunion and only a moment’s respite, Lula, Zeen, and their friends learned that the Nihil Stormwall has encroached further into Republic Space. Now, the team of young heroes prepare to defend the planet Eriadu, and the Republic at large, from an impending Nihil invasion!
